LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 3.3.1 PRONOUNS (‘I, YOU’)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Language use 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’), part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do you use the pronouns “I, and “you” to talk about yourself?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner’s ability to speak is enhanced as they use facts and examples to support own opinion in a conversation

using the pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you’.

● Digital literacy: The learner’s ability to interact with digital devices with assistive technology to record a conversation between family

members using the pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you’ during a role play.

Values:
• Love: A learner understands and appreciates the other’s opinions as they work together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem): The learner’s esteem is nurtured as they use the pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you ‘to talk about members of the family.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Concepts of pronouns ‘I’ and ‘you’ are learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous languages.

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards

• Appropriate reference materials in print

• Braille reference materials
